catalog_quote: The most frequent syllable types in Laboya is CV, although V and CVC-syllable types are also possible in certain positions. Length for all vowels is usually distinctive in the first stem syllable (i.e. in the first syllable that follows the derivational prefix, if any). The vowel in the second stem syllable is only long if stressed. [p. 18] ... (19) ... c. ngalung ‘wave’ [ˈŋaluŋ] CV-CVC [p. 25] ... All Laboyan clitics meet these criteria, as they are never stressed and can be hosted by different lexical categories. [p. 32] ... The vowel in the second stem syllable is only long if stressed.' p. 79 = printed p. 74, section 6 Conclusions: 'The possible syllable types in Laboya are V,…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the first syllable of the stem, i.e. the first syllable after any derivational prefix (prefix ka- is always unstressed and short, e.g. kaɗagha [kaˈɗagha]; ɓagga [ˈɓaɡa]); if a later stem syllable has a long vowel, that long-vowel syllable is stressed instead ('or the first stem syllable with a long vowel'). Vowel length is distinctive chiefly in the first stem syllable and a second stem syllable is long only if stressed, so stress and length are interdependent. Clitics are never stressed. Domain is the morphological stem/word; the author gives no dedicated stress section, no instrumental evidence and no explicit exceptions.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated beyond the long-vowel clause; the p. 74 summary hedges with 'generally'. The wording leaves open whether a long vowel in a non-initial stem syllable attracts stress or whether stress is what licenses length there (p. 18: second stem syllable is long only if stressed) - potentially weight-sensitive within the stem, but the author's primary statement is initial stem syllable.
new_statements.domain_note: Word/stem level (stem = root minus derivational prefixes); based on nine weeks of fieldwork (questionnaires and narratives) in Laboya district, West Sumba; no phrase-level or citation-form discussion.
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes Laboya (= Lamboya, ISO lmy, glottocode lamb1273) as spoken in kecamatan Lamboya and the Patiala Dete / Harona Kala sub-districts of Lamboya Barat, West Sumba; author distinguishes Laboya from the neighbouring Gaura community (Ethnologue's 'Gaura dialect'); no dialect split within Laboya is described (Patiala vs Laboya Proper are treated as one language).
